rationale: The highest-ranked cluster was another day of the Alaska two-Sullivan Senate ballot probe (now a federal criminal probe), but yesterday's entry was about that same story, so drawing it again would repeat the picture without a new visual event. Pope Leo XIV becoming the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election was led by six outlets (AP via PBS, CBS, NYT, BBC, Axios, Boston Globe). It is a US national story with a clear, drawable action, so it is the focal story. The record $6.3bn Binance hack was also strong but does not fit the same scene, and its attribution is unconfirmed. No Boston story matched national significance. Only the mail-in vote is drawn. How he voted is not known and is not shown.

stories.name: Pope Leo XIV votes by mail in the US midterms
facts: The Holy See press office confirmed on Oct. 30 that Pope Leo XIV, born Robert Prevost in Chicago, cast a mail-in ballot in Illinois ahead of the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. He is the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election.
The Chicago Sun-Times first reported the vote, citing the Will County clerk's office, which said he requested the mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. He is registered at an address in New Lenox, Illinois.
The Vatican said he has voted whenever he was eligible, including while living in Peru. Who he voted for is not known.

people.name: Pope Leo XIV
people.verified_action: cast a mail-in ballot in the Illinois midterm election from the Vatican; drawn in his white cassock and skullcap holding a sealed ballot envelope, with no visible marks or choices

stories.visual_notes: Clearly illustrative staging: Leo, in white cassock and white zucchetto, seen from behind or in profile at a Vatican balcony at dusk, sends off a plain sealed envelope. Its dotted flight path arcs over the Atlantic to a Chicago skyline at night (Willis Tower, the Hancock Center). No text on the envelope or ballot, no candidates, parties, marks or results, no crowds and no medical references.
stories.confidence: high: confirmed by the Holy See press office and reported independently by AP (via PBS NewsHour) and CBS News, which also confirmed the ballot request with the Will County clerk.
